title: Propeller Pitch System
description: The pitch linkage as five rigid bodies and their joints, with the two end stops, at 72 degrees blade pitch; no tolerances yet. Model v2; v1 is the legacy whole-system model.

provenance.structure_source: Jeff's forge note 20261108T001814_kpoev0 (2026-11-08): 'a new, simpler version of the model, focusing on just the kinematic end stop tolerance', each rigid body a chained stack, 'a single blade, pitch link, and tangential link to start out', and every correct 3D body including the piston cover.
provenance.joints_source: The P2 linkage sweep, data/inbox/linkage-sweeps/vpa-pitch-p2-20261105-204957.json: its geometry.features name ten of this document's nodes by body, under v1's ids, which is why every id here that v1 has is v1's.
provenance.ids: Every node id and every edge id v1 (`vpa_pitch_linkage`) also has names the same feature there; `ids_from` declares it (docs/DAG_TOPOLOGY.md, "Models").

bodies.name: ground
bodies.note: The hub, the two mounts and the piston cover, as a stack: the tangential link mount seats on the hub, the gas-spring mount on the tangential link mount (`tan_link_mount_gas_spring_seat`; Jeff, 2026-11-10: 'mount on mount'), and the piston cover's flange on the gas-spring mount (`piston_cover_mount_flange_seat`). Each of the three joints is a seat, a locating boss in a bore and a fastener pattern (Jeff, 2026-11-10: 'the same datum style with a flange, central locating boss, and fastener pattern for clocking'). linkage's base lists the first three parts alone; the difference is declared beside the pairing test.

bodies.name: tangential link
bodies.note: The 212956-005 assembly and its two bearings. Both bearings are pressed into the 212956-005 assembly, so they move with it and name it as their `parent` (2026-11-14, a_part_may_contain_parts); linkage lists the assembly alone because its mesh already draws them -- the difference v1 declares.

bodies.name: pitch plate
bodies.note: The plate, the gas-spring piston and the two piston heads. The two piston heads are the plate's: the lower sits on the piston body's shoulder (`piston_body_head_seat`) and the upper stacks on it (`piston_heads_seat`). The plate seats and is bolted on the piston body's flange about its pilot boss; one spigot on the piston body locates both heads, and the upper head is bolted to the piston body through the lower head's bore (2026-11-17, read off the meshes). linkage's pitch plate lists the first two parts alone; the difference is declared beside the pairing test.

bodies.name: pitch link
bodies.note: The 213862-002 assembly and its bearing, which names it as its `parent` (2026-11-14, a_part_may_contain_parts): the bearing is in the link assembly and in the link's body, and its tolerances come from its datasheet (Jeff).

bodies.name: blade 1
bodies.note: Blade 1 and its pitch arm: the arm's ring seats on the blade root's fitting, on its boss, clocked by one radial hole through both (2026-11-17, read off the meshes).

notes: Studyless by design for now: M2 adds one term per body and the end-stop study over them (dispatch/docs/strategy/drafts/DRAFT_tolerance_analysis_over_the_kinematic_model.md, '2026-11-08 -- the reset').
No edge carries a dimension. Each says what would close it; an untraced zero would read as a measured one.
Left out, on purpose: the gas spring, the VPA and its piston, the ring gear, the hydraulic brake, every fastener, washer and bushing, and blades 2 to 5. v1 keeps all of them.

Named once, 2026-11-10 (handoff the_model_is_derived_once_and_the_left_column_is_its_tree): a feature's name says the feature and not the part it is nested under; a feature two parts share names the seated part; a dimension is <from> to <to> in those words; one spelling of each term (locating boss, end stop, tangential link).

Edge order, 2026-11-10 (handoff the_gas_spring_mount_sits_on_the_tan_link_mount_in_the_end_stop_model): the walk is authored, and the hub's edges read its joint with the tangential link mount before its blade bore, so the base reads up the stack from the hub. With the blade bore first the parts drawn as blocks crossed once more than the builder's walk.
